did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with David’s personal commitment to exalt and bless the Lord—not only now, but forever and ever.
Did you know? This verse emphasizes that the Lord’s greatness cannot be fully understood: “His greatness is unsearchable.”
Did you know? According to the psalm, passing on praise for the Lord is an intergenerational responsibility: one generation praises His works and tells the next about His mighty acts.
Did you know? This verse describes the Lord through four central qualities: gracious, compassionate, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love.
Did you know? This verse extends the Lord’s goodness and compassion to “all His works,” meaning all creation described in the psalm.
Did you know? The praise focuses not only on the Lord’s goodness, but also on “the glory of His kingdom” and the power of His reign.
Did you know? The Lord’s kingdom is described as everlasting, while His dominion endures “throughout all generations.”
Did you know? The psalm portrays all creatures as looking to the Lord and waiting for Him to give them their food “at the proper time.”
Did you know? The Lord’s nearness in this verse is connected to sincere prayer: He is near “to all who call on Him in truth.”
Did you know? The psalm’s conclusion expands the circle of praise from the psalmist to “all flesh,” expressing the hope that every living being will bless the Lord’s name forever and ever.
